name: Plumbeous Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru (cusco) to western bolivia and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher of Andean slopes; rare in southern Peru, more common in Bolivia and northern Argentina. Male is separated from White-winged Black-Tyrant by grayer, less glossy plumage and from Cinereous Tyrant by darker belly.

name: Black-browed Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Eastern siberia to northern china and northern manchuria; winters to southern asia
description: Dull brown reed warbler with a sharply marked head, found in a variety of wetland habitats with substantial vegetation cover. Namesake black brow line is not always apparent, but the thick and strikingly pale supercilium is distinctive in its clean-cut and squared-off appearance.

name: Inca Wren
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (cusco)
description: Boldly patterned wren with a localized range in southern Peru. Reddish brown, with a black-and-white streaked face and breast and a bold white eyebrow.

name: Long-bearded Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Alpine grassland of east-central new guinea
description: A long, slender honeyeater of subalpine forest and shrubland in eastern New Guinea. All sooty gray-black plumage with long tail and very long, thin, curved bill, long white, whispy beard from the base of the bill, and a yellow-orange wattle at the back of the eye.

name: Dusky Fantail
rangeDescription: Makira (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Small, with a long, often fanned brown tail tipped with white and a cream-colored undertail. Mostly brown with a slightly darker head, a limited white throat, and two buffy wingbars.

name: Red-eared Firetail
rangeDescription: Southwestern western australia eastward to about esperance
description: Plump, tiny, short-tailed bird, olive above, blackish with white-spotted belly below, with a bright red bill. Very dark between eyes and bill (lores), with a pale eyering and a tiny red patch behind the eye.

name: Rust-and-yellow Tanager
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru to bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Small, bright yellow tanager of middle and high elevations. Males have a rusty orange head, while females have only a hint of rusty color, and immatures are plain yellow.

name: Taiwan Partridge
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: Subtly patterned sphere of a bird; the only hill partridge (genus Arborophila) on Taiwan, where endemic. Black-and-white facial pattern is diagnostic, unlikely to be confused with any other native bird.

name: Bronze Parotia
rangeDescription: North-central new guinea (foja mountains)
description: A fairly large, short-tailed bird of mid-mountane forest canopy in the Foja Mountains. Male is mainly black with white flanks, bronzy-scaled chest and 6 antennalike feathers projecting from the back of the head.

name: Fulvous-dotted Treerunner
rangeDescription: Western andes of colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: A uniquely-marked little Furnariid. Very uncommon in restricted range on the west slope of the Andes in Colombia and Ecuador.

name: Ibera Seedeater
rangeDescription: Breeds in northern argentina (iberá wetlands of corrientes), also reported paraguay and southern brazil
description: Very localized and poorly-known seedeater. Mostly known from northeastern Argentina and southern Paraguay, but also a disjunct cluster of records in Bolivia.

name: Pink-backed Pelican
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa and madagascar
description: Small by pelican standards, though still a very large bird! Adult is mostly pale gray with a pinkish bill and (in breeding plumage) a gray crest.

name: Aberdare Cisticola
rangeDescription: West-central kenya (aberdare mountains)
description: A large and relatively colorful cisticola endemic to Kenya, found locally in montane grassland and moorland. The cap and back of the neck are dull rufous with darker streaking, the back is heavily streaked with black, and there is a rufous panel in the wings.

name: Yellow-winged Vireo
rangeDescription: Montane forest of costa rica and western panama (western chiriquí)
description: Small yellowish bird; note bold wingbars and face pattern with short pale eyebrow and arc under the eye. Yellow underparts sometimes bright, sometimes paler whitish, but always some yellow tones.

name: Red-headed Quelea
rangeDescription: Grassland of sub-saharan africa
description: The red head of the breeding male is distinctive. Non-breeding male and female are nondescript, streaky brown birds with buffy eyebrows.

name: Rufous-tailed Shama
rangeDescription: Southern thai-malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Stout shama with a broad, black-tipped, orangish tail. Male has a dark gray upper body, small white eyebrow, and orangish rump and belly.

name: Ashy Woodswallow
rangeDescription: India and sri lanka to myanmar, southern china, and southeastern asia
description: A chunky, large-headed bird of open areas, usually found perched on wires or flying around in search of insects. Soft gunmetal gray with white underparts.

name: Chestnut-capped Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Campos of interior eastern and south-central brazil to northeastern paraguay
description: Large foliage-gleaner with startling yellow eyes and a long bill and tail. Rather uniform rufous above and paler below.

name: Whistling Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: The guianas and brazil north of the amazon river (from rio negro eastward to amapá)
description: Fairly small, warm brown woodcreeper with buffy spots on breast and vague buffy eyebrow. Note relatively short, straight bill.

name: Sulphur-bellied Tyrant-Manakin
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern peru to northern bolivia and adjacent western amazonian brazil
description: Large, tan manakin. Longer-tailed with a more upright posture than other smaller manakins.
